reason: The pancreatic islet sits beside glucose-rich blood, suggesting its cells sense the post-meal change.
expectation: The sensing cells should respond to the higher blood glucose, likely by releasing insulin.

effect: The post-meal signal produces insulin that reaches both muscle and liver, so I can follow its effects on either tissue.
reaction: The separate branches make the hormone's targets clear.
reason: The liver receives insulin and has glycogen machinery, making it a plausible place to store meal glucose.
expectation: The liver should take up and store some glucose as glycogen.

alternatives.reason: Muscle is also shown receiving insulin and could respond to it.

effect: Insulin favours liver glycogen storage and reduces glucose output; muscle remains the other shown target.
reaction: The distinction from muscle-style transporter insertion is useful.
reason: Skeletal muscle is the other tissue shown receiving the post-meal insulin signal.
expectation: Insulin should promote glucose uptake by muscle, with some glucose available for use or storage.

effect: Insulin increases muscle glucose uptake, and the post-meal goal is complete; the remaining goal concerns the period between meals.
reaction: The weakening insulin signal makes the feedback clearer.
reason: The pancreatic sensing cells can respond to the lower-glucose conditions between meals.
expectation: The islet should release a signal, likely glucagon, that helps maintain blood glucose.

effect: Lower glucose led to glucagon release, with the liver highlighted as its target.
reaction: The contrast between alpha-cell and beta-cell responses is clear.
reason: The liver contains glycogen and is shown receiving glucagon between meals.
expectation: Glucagon should promote glycogen breakdown and glucose release into the blood.

effect: Glucagon promotes liver glycogen breakdown and glucose release, with its stimulation diminishing as blood glucose rises; both goals are complete.
reaction: The feedback completes the contrast with the post-meal response clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing insulin’s effects on liver storage and muscle uptake was most worthwhile: the planned pictures distinguish liver glucose entry from the increased membrane transporters in muscle.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two pancreatic sensing combinations were predictable from the item titles and repeated the same basic selection, though they established the contrasting conditions.

surprise.text: The explicit distinction between liver glucose entry and muscle transporter insertion sharpened my understanding of how the tissues respond differently to insulin.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the choices followed the pictured hormone targets and the two glucose conditions.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose another chapter to see more system-level feedback explained through contrasting conditions, although these planned illustrations alone cannot establish how well students would understand it.
